findings.location: Paragraph containing Acts 4:20 (source.html third full paragraph after Matthew 9)
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the author’s meaning of “silenced” (i.e., rendered unable to speak because they were killed). In Afrikaans use a verb that unambiguously conveys “silenced” or “made unable to speak” (for example, “toe is hulle stilgemaak — deur die dood” or “later is hulle stilgemaak — deur die dood”). Replace the current phrasing with that wording, preserving surrounding HTML and punctuation.
findings.translation_quote: Later is hulle geswiep—deur die dood.

findings.location: Paragraph quoting Romans 8:36 (source.html paragraph that begins “I ordered a copy of The Martyr’s Mirror”)
findings.source_quote: As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the Scripture line so it faithfully conveys the English text. The current Afrikaans phrasing “Van julle weë word ons elke dag gedood” is inaccurate. Use a standard, faithful Afrikaans rendering that preserves the sense and placement of the verse (for example: “Soos geskrywe staan, ter wille van julle word ons elke dag gedood; ons word as skape tot die slagting getel.”). Ensure the quotation marks and verse placement remain as in the source, and keep the citation notation (Romans 8:36) unchanged elsewhere in the article.
findings.translation_quote: “Soos geskrywe staan, Van julle weë word ons elke dag gedood; ons word as skape tot die slagter getelb.”
